name: Science of Rules
title: Toward a Science of Rules: Can AI Change the Dynamics of Their Evolution?
tagline: Understanding how rules evolve. Exploring what AI changes.
intro: Science of Rules investigates how rules emerge, spread, change, and disappear. This six-month exploratory project treats rules as interacting populations and asks when AI-assisted rulemaking strengthens institutional error correction, and when faster production outpaces scrutiny, allowing errors and concentrated authority to accumulate across evolving institutions.
question: Can institutions keep learning as AI accelerates rule-making?
question_text: Rules carry ideas across institutions. They are copied, revised, contested, and retired. We study these processes together to understand when institutions remain capable of correcting their own mistakes.
overview: This SNU Grand Quest project investigates how rules emerge, spread, change, and disappear, and how AI may alter these processes. The six-month exploratory plan prioritizes a pilot Rule Observatory and preliminary studies of rule dynamics, with prediction benchmarks and simulation designs providing foundations for follow-up research.

proposals.heading: Share a research proposal.
proposals.invitation: We welcome collaboration ideas, relevant datasets, methodological suggestions, and domain expertise on the evolution of rules and AI-assisted rulemaking.
proposals.prompt: Tell us about your idea, how it connects to this project, and the collaboration you have in mind.
